1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 48:  p300.dispense(4, reaction_well)
   The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the
     map verifies; the plate is the problem.
   Affected: wells A1, A10, A11, A12, A2, A3, A4, A5 and 16 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html

           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html

           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 1 ul of dntp and 8 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 12 wells never mixed after water went in (25% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 59 the robot added water to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 4, which already held buffer, rt, dntp, primers and 12 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 4 after line 59: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 63 the tip touched the liquid in tube A3 in slot 2 while it still carried rna 1 (well A1 in slot 3), rna 2 (well A2 in slot 3), rna 3 (well A3 in slot 3), rna 4 (well A4 in slot 3) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 22 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 14 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 63, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: rna 1 (well A1 in slot 3)
findings.explanation: At line 67 the tip went into rna 1 (well A1 in slot 3) while it still carried water (tube A5 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 67 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
